# Intent-gate ground truth — the prompts cmd/forge/intent.go's threshold is derived from.
#
# B-033 pairs the neighbour floor with intent.go's hardcoded 0.7 because both were
# calibrated against the pre-B-008 scale. They share a root cause, not an answer: the two
# gates have opposite cost functions. A neighbour false positive is one wrong wikilink in
# a note under review. An intent false positive interrupts a user prompt with injected
# context, on every prompt, in a hook contracted never to disturb the session. So this
# gate is derived for precision where the floor is derived for recall.
#
# FIRE  — the vault genuinely already answers this; surfacing the hit is the point.
#         Each is phrased as a user would type it, against a note that exists.
# QUIET — the vault does not answer this. Adjacent-topic prompts, which are exactly the
#         hard negatives (a related note exists and scores), plus off-corpus prompts,
#         which must never fire.
#
# Written from the corpus slug list before any score was measured, same rule as
# neighbour-labels.txt.
